newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark objective at 1.8610, for now.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark objective at 1.8610, for now.

text.p: Dollar/mark, having surged to its highest since November 1989, has enough stamina left to lock in on a 1.8610 objective, analysts said on Monday.
Dollar/mark cleared 1.8430, the 1991 peak, to surge to 1.8490, its highest since November 1989 when that pair surged to 1.8690. A close above 1.8430 would help meet that goal.

"We are looking at 1.8610, the objective in a rising channel from November 1996," said I.D.E.A. analyst Ben Morden, who did not expect much resistance until 1.9310, the June 1989 low. Morden also pointed out that dollar/mark went through breath-taking moves in May/June that year.
Dollar/mark shot up nearly 17 pfennigs or 9.0 percent during those two months, from a low of 1.8797 in May to a cycle's high of 2.0478 in June.

Analysts pointed out it was difficult to project where the 1997 dollar/mark rally would stop since chart gaps were less relevant over a span of several years. Again, uncertainty about much Europe was willing to let its currencies depreciate to launch the euro in 1999 weighed on the mark.
An added plus for the dollar outlook was that the yen finally joined in the rally long focused on dollar/Europe, analysts also said.
Dollar/yen took out a key resistance at 117.00 late on Friday and again on Monday to hit a 10-week high of 117.78.
The next key level is 119.00, the 50-percent retracement of the 126.47/110.62 high/low move in 1997.
The 38-percent retracement of that move was 117.00 which also coincided with the 200-day moving average and with a key chart level on a rising trendline from September 1995.

"This is a good sign because so far, there was little correlation between dollar/yen and dollar/mark," Morden noted. "Now, it is the dollar's side of the rally, not just the dollar picking up the slack from the weak mark."
Morden said one drag on dollar/mark may come from a sharp sterling correction which would end the need for dollar hedging of sterling/mark and thus weaken dollar/mark.

But analysts also said noted that dollar/Swiss action -- that pair soared to a near-four-year high of 1.5250 -- augured well for dollar/mark, which would find help in a breach 0.82 support on mark/Swiss.
Morden noted mark/Swiss gave a first sign of weakness last week when it dipped below 0.8080, a near-breach of a rising trendline from the all-time low of 0.7975 in September 1995.
